Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Novena's security and procurement teams have signalled positive intent to proceed with a private deployment (VPC or on-prem — final topology depends on your ops guidance). Before the procurement team prepares a PO, we need to confirm a few privacy/DPA items and operator access boundaries: 

- Customer-managed key options: we need confirmation that customer CMKs can remain in our HSM (AWS CloudHSM) and that Redwood will not be able to decrypt any customer-owned keys.
- Operator access: please confirm what operator-level access Redwood engineers require for day-to-day support and what will be strictly prohibited (e.g., plaintext model inputs, batch exports).
- Subprocessors & transfers: list of subprocessors and whether any processing occurs outside the US; if so, what safeguards (SCCs) apply.
- Escrow & recovery: if we lose keys, what's the supported recovery path? Will escrow be available and under what controls?

I've attached a short BYOK Q&A and a redlined DPA; legal will expect written answers we can attach to the contract. Can we schedule a 30-minute call with your security/ops team tomorrow or Monday?

Attachments: BYOK_Q&A.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), Novena_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marcus (serving/runtime lead) and Soojin (legal) so we can answer both the technical and contractual points.

Quick notes before the call:
- We fully support customer-kept CMKs (BYOK) in both VPC and on-prem topologies. Customer CMKs remain under customer control; Redwood operates against wrapped keys or uses a split-key model in on-prem scenarios.
- For operator access, we typically limit support to metadata, telemetry, and orchestrator-level control plane actions. Any request to access plaintext data requires an established breakglass process (audited, time-limited, customer approval).
- Subprocessor list and geography: we'll bring the up-to-date list and clarify any EU/third-country data flow.
- Escrow: we have an optional sealed-escrow workflow for extremely high-impact cases; it requires customer initiation and multi-party approval.

I've attached a high-level architecture diagram and a short playbook excerpt that outlines the breakglass and escrow workflow. Proposed call slots: 2027-04-25 09:00 or 11:30 PT. Which works for you?

Hi Samantha — technical follow-up from my side (short bullet points to populate your Q&A):

1) Keys & cryptography
- VPC (cloud-hosted): recommended pattern is customer-kept CMK in their CloudHSM or KMS with HSM-backed keys. Redwood will use wrapped DEKs; we never store raw CMKs.
- On-prem: we support HSM appliances (PKCS#11) mounted into the runtime. In on-prem, we can run a split-signature protocol so Redwood holds a blinded shard only for liveness checks — shard alone cannot decrypt.
- Breakglass: operator-initiated breakglass requires explicit customer auth (signed SAML assertion or DocuSign approval), two Redwood approvers, and we produce an immutable audit bundle (timestamped logs + copies of approvals).

2) Operator access scope
- Allowed: deployment orchestration, instance health, non-content telemetry (token counts, latencies), and anonymized model trace sampling (hashed identifiers only).
- Prohibited: retrieval of raw request/response payloads, bulk exports of customer data, or any decryption of customer-protected content without the breakglass process.

3) Subprocessors & transfers
- Current subprocessors: monitoring (US), metrics backend (US), SRE partner for hardware maintenance (contracted US/EU facilities). We do not route request payloads to subprocessors for processing; only logs/metrics (configurable retention).
- If Novena requires SCCs or a BCR-like flow for EU transfers, we can execute SCCs and provide attestation.

4) Escrow & recovery
- Option A (recommended): Sealed escrow where customer uploads an encrypted backup of key material to a third-party escrow vault. Redwood can only retrieve under customer RESTORE request with signed approval.
- Option B: Redwood-managed ephemeral split-keys (customer rotation required every 90 days).

I'll bring a short one-pager and the subprocessors manifest to tomorrow's call.

Attachments referenced: BYOK_Q&A.xlsx (filled draft), subprocessors_manifest.csv

—Marcus

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from legal/procurement after reviewing your bullets and the redlined DPA: 

- DPA: we redlined a clause to explicitly state "Redwood will not access or attempt to access plaintext customer content except under the documented breakglass process" and added a definition for "breakglass". Can you confirm acceptance or propose language?
- Escrow: legal is reluctant to allow Redwood any unilateral retrieval. We would accept a sealed third-party escrow (only retrievable with a customer-signed request). Please confirm the escrow vendor options and whether Redwood will be present in the retrieval workflow.
- Subprocessors: we need the physical locations for your hardware maintenance partner; if they operate in APAC we will need extra contractual guarantees.
- Evidence: legal would like an example of the immutable audit bundle (sample redaction ok) and the retention window for telemetry/anonymized logs.

I've attached Novena_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf with comments inline. Can we confirm acceptance points in writing by EOD Monday so procurement can issue a PO?

Samantha

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novenahealth.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: BYOK handoff + operator access for private deploy

Samantha — thanks for the redlines and clear asks. High-level responses and proposed contract language we can accept: 

1) Plaintext access clause (proposed language): "Redwood shall not access, copy, or attempt to decrypt Customer Content except pursuant to the documented Breakglass Process initiated by Customer and authorized by at least two Redwood officers; any access under such process shall be limited to the minimum scope necessary and shall be accompanied by an immutable audit bundle delivered to Customer within 24 hours."

2) Sealed escrow: We agree to a third-party sealed escrow model. Redwood will be able to assist operationally in a retrieval only after: (a) Customer submits a signed retrieval request, (b) escrow provider confirms retrieval conditions, and (c) retrieval is logged and copies of the audit bundle are shared with Customer. Vendor options we recommend: KeyCustody LLC (US), SafeVault EU (EU).

3) Subprocessors & locations: Marcus will attach a manifest. Our hardware maintenance partner maintains facilities in US and EU only; no APAC footprint for those teams. We will include a contractual obligation to notify Novena of any subprocessor changes 30 days in advance.

4) Audit bundle & retention: sample bundle (redacted) can be provided in the next 48 hours. Default telemetry retention is 90 days; we can offer a reduced retention profile (30 days) for higher-sensitivity customers.

5) SCCs & transfers: we will execute EU SCC Addendum where applicable and include the SCCs by reference in the DPA.

Proposed next steps: 
- Marcus: please produce the subprocessors manifest and a redacted sample audit bundle by EOD 2027-04-27.
- Laura: confirm a PO timeline and whether Novena will elect VPC or on-prem for the initial deployment.

I'll incorporate the agreed language into the DPA once we confirm.

—Soojin Lee
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Samantha — great progress. Quick summary and commitments from Redwood: 

- Contract: Redwood accepts the plaintext/no-access clause as proposed by Soojin. We'll merge the clause into the DPA and return a near-final copy by 2027-04-30 EOD.
- Escrow: We will proceed with sealed escrow (KeyCustody LLC). Retrieval requires customer initiation and two Redwood approvers; Redwood's role is strictly operational during retrieval and never unilateral.
- Subprocessors: Marcus attached the manifest to the internal thread and confirmed US/EU-only maintenance. We'll include 30-day notice for subprocessor changes in the DPA.
- Evidence: Marcus will send a redacted audit bundle and the telemetry retention configuration by tomorrow.
- Next steps: if Novena approves these terms in writing, we will share a DocuSign packet for the DPA and SOW and coordinate an initial SRE runbook review week of 2027-05-03. Procurement, please confirm PO issuance target.
